title: Cernly scan output (facts.json) v1
description: Output of one extractor run on one commit. Deterministic: same commit + same extractor version = byte-identical file. Serialised as canonical JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS): sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace. No timestamps of the scan itself, no hostnames, no absolute paths. Draft until the first scan is stored; from then on only additive changes in v1.

committed_at.description: Committer date from git, UTC. Comes from the commit, so it is deterministic.

dirty.description: A checkout scan without --commit read tracked files with uncommitted changes, so the facts may not match sha. Absent when clean. Never stored.

extractor.description: The provider catalogue is a rules input; its version is in the map (https://cernly.dev/how/catalogue/)

plugins.description: Plugins that ran in this scan, sorted by name. An incremental scan lists only the plugins it re-ran.

name.description: Open set: built-in and WebAssembly plugins (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/)

sha256.description: Hash of the WebAssembly module; wasm only

signer.description: Key id that signed the module; wasm only

facts.description: Sorted by (kind, key), then evidence by (path, line).

key.description: Stable identity of the thing, independent of where it is written. Format <kind>:<source>:<name>; dependencies carry their manifest directory (dependency:go:worker:github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai) so two modules can pin different versions, transitive ones their lockfile folder and the lockfile's own identity (dependency:npm:.:lock:node_modules/qs, dependency:pypi:api:lock:starlette); compose services and data stores carry their stack (service:compose:production:api). Moving a line does NOT change the key.

attrs.description: Kind-specific attributes, see the attrs_* defs. Never contains secret or env values.

evidence.description: Every place in the repo that proves this fact. A fact without evidence is invalid.

workflow_ref.description: A CI job that reaches a command, directly or through scripts, tasks, make targets or npm scripts. Triggers and conditions are recorded as written; which branch really deploys is decided by rules.

after.description: workflow_run: workflows this one follows, by name

after_branches_ignore.description: workflow_run branches-ignore; absent when not written

conditions.description: if: of this job, of every job it needs and of the step that reaches the command, as written; all must hold

step.description: Set when the if: is a step's: its name:, else its id:, else #n counting from 1

branches.description: Push branch filters in written order; ["*"] = no branch or tag filter, [] = branches-ignore or tags only

branches_ignore.description: Push branches-ignore; absent when not written

tags.description: Push tags; absent when not written

tags_ignore.description: Push tags-ignore; absent when not written

job_line.description: Line of the job's key in the workflow file

step.description: Stacks and image builds: the step that reaches the command

steps_after.description: Stacks and image builds: every step of the job after that step, as written

starts.description: Stacks: a command of this job starts the stack (compose up, kubectl apply, helm upgrade); false when it only renders or validates it (helm template, kustomize build, compose config). Absent in scans from before 4 Nov

image_repo.description: Last literal path segment of the image name, no tag or registry

dockerfile_resolved.description: The Dockerfile path points to a tracked file

tags.description: Image references as written, templates kept

push.description: The build command itself pushes: build-push-action push: true (the action's default is false), --push, or --output with type=registry or push=true. True when any build command of this key does; false when every one is known not to; absent when one cannot be read (a template, bake). A later docker push step is judged by the rules from steps_after

attrs_image_recipe.description: What one buildable Dockerfile stage contains (https://cernly.dev/how/facts/). Key image_recipe:<dockerfile>:<target or _final>.

target.description: Stage name for --target; "_final" for an unnamed last stage

final.description: Last stage: what is built when no --target is given

base_images.description: Outside images this stage is built from, through FROM or COPY --from, following the stages it inherits or copies from. scratch is never listed.

raw.description: As written, only when ARG substitution changed it

stage.description: Stage that uses the image: its name, "_final" or "#<index>"

artifact.description: ref parsed; raw and templated from the reference as written

sources.description: Build-context paths copied in, directly or through COPY --from stages

remote_sources.description: URLs fetched by ADD at build time

entrypoints.description: Builds whose output ends up in this stage. Recorded now, used by binary-level links (v2).

path.description: go: package path, mapped to the repo when resolved

resolved.description: go: path maps back to the build context through a COPY line

attrs_agent_config.description: An AI coding tool the repo is set up for, from the configuration it leaves (.cursor/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,...); key agent_config:<tool>; every matching file is evidence. Repo-level proof, not proof of which commit it wrote.

attrs_owner.description: An owner the repo names (https://cernly.dev/how/ownership/). Key owner:<owner, lower case>. From the CODEOWNERS file the forge reads (.github/CODEOWNERS, then CODEOWNERS, then docs/CODEOWNERS; only the first tracked one); evidence is every line that names the owner. GitLab section owners count for the entries without their own.

owner.description: @user, @org/team or an email address, as written, lower case

patterns.description: The patterns this owner owns, in file order

default.description: Owns the whole repo by a * (or /, /*, **) entry

attrs_test_suite.description: Test files of one module by the language's convention (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/); key test_suite:<language>:<module folder>. Nothing is run or measured: no coverage. Evidence is the first 50 test files, sorted

path.description: The module folder: go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml / setup.py / requirements, pom.xml / build.gradle, the folder of a .NET test project (.csproj, .fsproj, .vbproj)

language.description: Open set; known: go, javascript (TypeScript included), python, java (Kotlin included), csharp, fsharp, vb

framework.description: From the module's declared dependencies: go-test, vitest, jest, mocha, playwright, cypress, pytest, unittest, junit5, junit4, testng, spock, kotest, xunit, nunit, mstest, tunit; unknown when nothing declares one

dirs.description: Folders that hold test files, sorted

attrs_test_run.description: A command that runs tests (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/), found by the command reader in workflows, scripts, Makefiles, Taskfiles and package.json scripts; key test_run:<tool>:<dir>. Whether a job ran on a change is the checks reader's (https://cernly.dev/how/catalogue/)

tool.description: Open set; known: go, npm, pnpm, yarn, jest, vitest, playwright, cypress, pytest, maven, gradle

dir.description: Folder it runs in: -C, --prefix, --dir, -f pom.xml, -p project, the folder of a package.json script, else the repo root

command.description: The first such command, as written, at most 200 characters

attrs_source_size.description: Source files and physical lines of one language in one folder, not its subfolders (size as context, https://cernly.dev/how/map/). Key source_size:<folder>:<language>, and source_size:<folder>:<language>:test for its test files by the language's convention (*_test.go; *.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/; test_*.py, *_test.py, conftest.py; src/test/, *Test.java, *IT.java; *_spec.rb; *Tests.cs (and .fs, .vb) and a folder ending in .Tests, .UnitTests, .IntegrationTests or .Specs; any folder named test, tests, spec, e2e or testdata). The language comes from the extension (go, typescript, javascript, python, java,...); markup, styles, data and configuration are not counted, nor minified bundles. Evidence: every counted file, line 1 to its last line.

test.description: The files are test code; absent otherwise

attrs_import.description: One package of the repo importing another package of the repo (the module graph, https://cernly.dev/how/map/). Key import:<language>:<from>:<to>. Go: from the parsed import declarations of non-test files, never go tooling; the target resolves by the longest module path of a go.mod in the repo, and must be a folder with Go files. .NET (dotnet): one per ProjectReference between two project files of the repo; from and to are the project file paths, from_dir and to_dir their folders. Imports of packages outside the repo are dependencies, not imports. Evidence: every import line (.NET: every ProjectReference line).

from_module.description: Go: the module path of the importing package

attrs_catalog_entity.description: A Backstage entity a catalog-info.yaml (or.yml) in the repo describes (https://cernly.dev/how/ownership/). Key catalog_entity:<kind>:<namespace>/<name>, lower case, as Backstage writes entity references. Only backstage.io apiVersions; Location entities and scaffolder skeletons (a ${{ }} name) are left out; a field that is still a placeholder is left out. Evidence: the kind and name lines and the line of each field read.

kind.description: component, system, domain, api, resource, group,...

owner.description: spec.owner as written (an entity reference or a name)

route_address.description: A site address or upstream as written, split where it is literal. A {$VAR} host is kept as the variable's name (host_env); its value is in the deployment, not the repo

attrs_route.description: One route of a web server config (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/): a site, a matcher and what handles it. Key route:<caddy|nginx>:<root file>:<first address>:<matcher>, route:traefik:<file>:<router>. nginx: one per server and location, the location as written with its modifier (= /x, ~ regex, ^~ /x) in paths, upstream blocks resolved to their servers, root/alias as file_server. Caddyfile snippets and imports are expanded into the root file that loads them; evidence points at the site line, any import lines, and the handler line, in the file that holds each. Global options are not read

file.description: The root config file, as a compose service mounts it

matcher.description: A named matcher (@name) that tests more than paths and methods

rule.description: traefik: the router rule as written; addresses, paths (PathPrefix as /x*) and methods are its positive matchers

labels_on.description: A route from container labels: the compose service that carries them (and the upstream)

proxy_image.description: With labels_on: the image name of the proxy that reads the labels; the routes rule finds it in each stack by that name

attrs_stack.description: A set of definition files a deploy tool combines (https://cernly.dev/how/stacks/). Emitted by invocation readers (phase 1) and, for files no invocation covers, by the tool adapter as a convention stack (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/). Key stack:<tool>:<name>. Which stack is production is decided by rules, not here.

source.description: convention: no invocation found, files grouped by the tool's naming rules; lower confidence

unresolved.description: Files not found as tracked files or templated

default_files.description: No -f given; compose's default file names were used

starts.description: At least one invocation starts containers (up, create, start, restart, run)

conditional_files.description: Files an invocation adds only under a condition the scan cannot decide (an append after `check || return 0`, or inside if, case or a loop). Not in files and not merged; recorded with the condition as written (https://cernly.dev/how/stacks/)

assumptions.description: What a link in the invocation chain assumes, in words: a remote command after a cd on another host is read from the repo root, assuming the host runs a checkout of this repo (https://cernly.dev/how/stacks/)

scan_config.description: Present when the repo's hint file (.cernly.yml, or a fallback name the calling application passed for commits from before it renamed its own) or the operator excluded or declared something. Every exclusion and declaration is visible to readers of the scan.

reincluded.description: Files this repo rule matched that the operator re-included

declared.description: What a person declared (https://cernly.dev/how/config/): never a fact; the rules apply it and show it as declared

gate.description: Gate levels per rule (https://cernly.dev/how/gate/), from both sides; the gate takes the stricter

licences.description: licence_not_allowed only: the licence ids it watches (https://cernly.dev/how/sbom/)

tags.description: key:value labels on the repo (https://cernly.dev/how/ownership/); per key the operator's entry replaces the repo's

ext.description: Plugin-specific detail. Never read by core rules or the map; the same no-secrets, no-values rule applies.

artifact_ref.description: A parsed image or package reference (https://cernly.dev/how/facts/).

templated.description: Variable names in the raw reference

pinning.description: digest: @sha256. exact: a full version (x.y.z) or a release date, variant suffix allowed. floating: latest, no tag, a major or major.minor, any other word. unknown: the tag comes from a variable without a default.

unit.description: Optional: Compose service, Go package or module the evidence belongs to. Used by the rule that links facts to services.

ecosystem.description: Open set; known: go, npm, pypi (names PEP 503-normalised), nuget

version.description: Exact version from the lockfile when available, else the declared range as written

version_info.description: version through the scheme parser (https://cernly.dev/how/facts/); ranges and workspace specs are unknown

internal.description: The dependency resolves to a folder of this repo (https://cernly.dev/how/facts/): an internal edge, never a third-party package

path.description: Repo folder of the package or module

spec.description: How it resolves: the npm spec as written (*, workspace:*, file:../x) or replace / go.work for Go

direct.description: false: a transitive dependency from a lockfile (https://cernly.dev/how/sbom/), or a Go // indirect requirement

scope.description: dev = devDependencies; runs in CI, not shipped. unknown until import analysis decides (Go). Transitive: the lockfile's dev flag, else prod when a prod dependency of some root reaches it

license.description: The licence as the lockfile declares it (npm); absent when nothing declares one. Never looked up

lockfile.description: Transitive only: the lockfile (or go.mod) that records it

roots.description: Transitive only: manifest folders that reach it through another package

via.description: Transitive only: names of the packages that require it, as the lockfile records; empty when the lockfile has no graph

stack.description: Name of the stack this fact belongs to; the stack fact's key is stack:<tool>:<stack>

build_context.description: Repo-relative folder; links the service to its code

dockerfile.description: Repo path of the Dockerfile its build: names (default Dockerfile in the context)

mounts.description: Bind mounts of tracked repo files (sources resolve against the project folder, merged by target across files). Named volumes, directories, absolute paths and untracked files are left out

stack.description: Name of the stack this fact belongs to

version.description: From the image tag: the normalised version (17, 2025-04-22T22:12:26Z)

version_info.description: The tag through the version scheme parser (https://cernly.dev/how/facts/); raw is the full tag

attrs_env_var.description: One fact per name across the repo; every place it appears is evidence (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/). Compose evidence carries the service as unit, Go evidence the module folder.

name.description: Name only. Values are dropped inside the plugin.

origins.description: Sorted, unique. config: a tool's config file reads it when the tool loads (Caddyfile {$VAR} and {env.VAR}, Prisma env("…"))

host_hints.description: Host part only, from example values that are URLs with a public hostname (e.g. api.mollie.com). No scheme, credentials, port or path. Sorted, unique.

attrs_outbound_host.description: One fact per public host Go code points at (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/); every place is evidence, unit = module folder

host.description: Lower-case hostname, no port, no path

usage.description: Strongest proven use: request = reaches a net/http request in the same package; default = a configured URL (a name ending in URL/Endpoint/Host, or an env lookup default); mention = any other literal

attrs_db_table.description: A table a schema source declares. Prisma (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/): key db_table:prisma:<schema folder>:<name>, one per model, named by @@map and @@schema (public for PostgreSQL when none); views and composite types are not tables. Evidence spans the model block. SQL migrations (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/): key db_table:sql:<migration set folder>:<name>, the tables the set leaves after replaying it in order (public when unqualified only in a set the SQL or a Prisma migration_lock.toml shows to be PostgreSQL, names as written otherwise; ext.dialect, ext.dialect_signal and ext.dialect_at say which and where); evidence is the creating statement and every later statement that changed the table. EF Core migrations (https://cernly.dev/how/plugins/): key db_table:efcore:<migrations folder>:<context>:<schema.name>, the tables left after replaying the Up methods in migration id order; the schema is the schema argument, else the provider's default (dbo for SQL Server, public for PostgreSQL), else none with ext.provider_unknown; ext.context, ext.provider and ext.provider_at name the DbContext and the provider package

name.description: schema.table, or table where the engine has no schemas

model.description: Prisma: the model name, when @@map renames the table

rls.description: Row-level security enabled in migrations (SQL: true or false after replaying the full set). Absent when the source cannot say (a Prisma schema, a MySQL set, a set of no known dialect), never false by default

attrs_db_column.description: A column a schema source declares. Prisma: one per field the database stores (relation fields and composite types are left out), named by @map; key db_column:prisma:<schema folder>:<table>.<column>. SQL migrations: key db_column:sql:<migration set folder>:<table>.<column>; evidence is where the column got its definition and later changes. EF Core migrations: key db_column:efcore:<migrations folder>:<context>:<schema.name>.<column>; type is the CLR type of table.Column<T>, native_type the type: argument, ext.max_length the maxLength: argument

type.description: As the source writes it: Prisma's scalar type, an enum's name, [] for lists, Unsupported("…"); SQL: the type as written, lower case with spacing normalised (varchar(320), timestamp with time zone), a quoted type name as written

enum.description: The type is an enum the schema declares (its values are not stored)

primary_key.description: Part of the primary key (@id or @@id)

native_type.description: The database type when given (@db.VarChar(320) as VarChar(320))

rule.description: Detector rule id, e.g. generic-api-key. The secret itself is never stored, hashed or fingerprinted.
